title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
pdf_path: papers/GuardAgent_Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning.pdf
threat_model_summary: A separate guardrail agent inspects the target agent's input/output logs against natural-language safety requests and agent specifications; violations are rejected. Not a cryptographic adversary model; the target agent and policy author are trusted.
core_contributions: GuardAgent: independent guardrail agent with memory-based planning and code generation
EICU-AC benchmark (316 cases) and Mind2Web-SC benchmark (200 cases)
>=98.4% and >=83.5% label accuracy across four core LLMs
Target agent task success preserved at 100% in reported settings
limitations: Guardrail is itself an LLM and can be wrong or injected
Policy expressed in natural language; no formal semantics
Benchmarks limited to healthcare DB and web scenarios
Latency/cost of an extra agent not fully characterized
No cryptographic mechanism
theoretical_crypto_links: None; no security definition or proof
Policy enforcement is LLM reasoning, not cryptographic authorization
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, tokens or TEE
Could be combined with signed policies/scoped credentials, but not implemented (our inference)

title: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents
pdf_path: papers/SafeArena_Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Evaluates deliberate misuse of web agents by users issuing harmful tasks, with paired safe tasks. Harm is judged by an LLM evaluator and human annotations; no cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: SafeArena: 250 harmful and 250 paired safe tasks on four WebArena-based sites
ARIA four-level risk framework and normalized safety score NSS
Human annotation of 150 harmful tasks
Shows weak transfer of chat safety alignment to web agents, including decomposition jailbreaks
limitations: LLM-judge scoring and limited human annotation
Four sandbox websites may not cover the open web
Task construction may embed annotator bias
No formal safety definition
No cryptographic mechanism
theoretical_crypto_links: None; benchmark and judge, not a security definition
applied_crypto_links: Only a downstream behavior test for guardrails (our inference)

title: AdvAgent: Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents
pdf_path: papers/AdvAgent_Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Attacker can modify HTML but has no access to the agent framework, weights or logits. The attack keeps the rendered operation and element while replacing arguments, aiming for a controllable, visually stealthy adversarial action.
core_contributions: Controllable black-box red-teaming of web agents via HTML attribute injection
GPT-4 candidate generation plus SFT/DPO prompter training
97.5% ASR on SeeAct+GPT-4V and 99.8% on Gemini 1.5
Controllability and stealthiness evaluation, plus prompt-defense tests
limitations: Requires offline feedback from the victim agent
Single-step ASR, no end-to-end task evaluation
Limited cross-backend transfer (18%)
Only HTML-attribute injection surface
No formal security model
theoretical_crypto_links: None; black-box means no weights/logits, not a cryptographic black box
Stealthiness is rendered equivalence, not computational indistinguishability
applied_crypto_links: Signed DOM/SRI attestation is at most a peripheral integrity control (our inference)

title: Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory
pdf_path: papers/Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory.pdf
threat_model_summary: Black-box attacker interacts with an agent and issues crafted prompts (locator + aligner) to extract records from the agent's long-term memory; no access to memory files or model weights. No cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: MEXTRA black-box memory extraction attack
Locator+aligner prompt decomposition and automatic prompt generation
Evaluation on EHRAgent and RAP across memory/retrieval configurations
Shows edit-distance retrieval and larger memory increase leakage
limitations: Single-agent, static memory setting
No session control; multi-user sharing not evaluated
Defenses only discussed qualitatively
No formal privacy definition
No cryptographic mechanism
theoretical_crypto_links: None; empirical privacy leakage, not cryptographic privacy
Memory confidentiality leakage bounds and per-session keys are our inference
applied_crypto_links: At-rest encryption does not help because records must enter the prompt in plaintext (our inference)
No TEE, access control or key management implemented

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
pdf_path: papers/The Task Shield_Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Indirect prompt injection in tool outputs; a Task Shield checks whether each action contributes to the user's original task. The checker is an LLM and is not a cryptographic reference monitor.
core_contributions: Task Alignment definition and Task Shield runtime guardrail
Reduces AgentDojo targeted ASR from 47.69% to 2.07% on GPT-4o
Evaluates utility, latency and ablations
Shows input-only shield as a cheaper tradeoff
limitations: Depends on LLM extraction and scoring; proof-of-concept
Large latency overhead (median 6.17s to 62.56s in Slack)
User-level messages unconditionally trusted
Single trial per task, no confidence intervals
No adaptive attack evaluation
theoretical_crypto_links: None; task alignment is semantic, not cryptographic authorization
Signed task-scoped credentials plus hard policy checks are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No keys, signatures, MACs, TEE or proofs
Task-scoped policy could be enforced by a gateway, but not implemented
